subject: physics
question_text: At what temperature does the rms speed of the molecules of a gas become double its value at 0°C, at constant pressure?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Very Short Answer Question 15 (printed p.138). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: v_rms ∝ √T, so doubling v_rms requires T to become 2² = 4 times as large; starting from T₁ = 0°C = 273 K, T₂ = 4 × 273 = 1092 K, arithmetic verified.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. State v_rms ∝ √T before jumping to the factor of 4.
steps.why: Since v_rms is proportional to the square root of T, the ratio of two rms speeds equals the square root of the ratio of their absolute temperatures; making v_rms twice as large therefore needs T to become 2² = 4 times as large.
common_mistakes: Assuming doubling v_rms means doubling T directly. The relation is a square root, not a straight proportion.
Forgetting that T must be the absolute temperature, not the Celsius value.

recall.must_convey: That the rms speed is proportional to the square root of the absolute temperature, so doubling it needs T to become 4 times as large.
accept: v rms proportional to root T
doubling v rms needs T times 4
square the speed ratio to get the temperature ratio
heard_as: v rms proportional to root T

steps.memory_tip: v_rms goes as √T — to double a square root, the number inside must go up by 2² = 4.

steps.label: Temperature value
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Convert 0°C to 273 K first, then multiply by 4.
steps.why: T₁ = 273 K is 0°C converted to the absolute scale, so multiplying by the factor of 4 found in the first step gives the temperature at which the rms speed is double its value at 0°C.
common_mistakes: Using 0°C as 0 K instead of converting it to 273 K on the absolute scale.
Reporting 1092°C instead of 1092 K, or not converting the final answer back to Celsius when it is asked for.

recall.must_convey: That starting from 273 K at 0°C, the required temperature is 4 times 273, which is 1092 K.
reject: v rms proportional to root T

steps.memory_tip: Convert first: 0°C = 273 K. Then just multiply by the factor of 4 from the relation.

insider_note: Always convert 0°C to 273 K before multiplying — a student who multiplies 0°C × 4 gets zero and loses the second mark.
